CRITICAL Issues\n\n### Issue 1: Device ID Changes Every Refresh (Breaking Low-Battery Notifications)\n**File:** `BatteryService.swift:65`\n\n```swift\nlet device = DeviceBattery(\n    id: UUID().uuidString,  // New UUID every time = new device every time\n    ...\n)\n```\n\n**Problem:** Every time `detectDevices()` runs, it creates a new `UUID` for the same physical device. This breaks `NotificationService.notifiedDevices` tracking (line 36-38) because the device ID used as notification identifier changes, so notifications will fire every refresh cycle instead of once until recharged.\n\n**Fix:** Derive device ID from stable properties (e.g., product name + device type hash), not UUID.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 2: Service Instances Not Shared in AppDelegate\n**File:** `MagicMouseBatteryApp.swift:25-26`\n\n```swift\nprivate var notificationService: NotificationService { NotificationService() }\nprivate var launchAtLoginService: LaunchAtLoginService { LaunchAtLoginService() }\n```\n\n**Problem:** These computed properties create **new instances** each access. The `@StateObject` in `App` creates one instance, but `AppDelegate` creates separate instances — state is not shared.\n\n**Fix:** Store the shared service references or access `BatteryService.shared` pattern consistently.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 3: Hardened Runtime Disabled\n**File:** `project.yml:27`\n\n```yaml\nENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME: NO\n```\n\n**Problem:** Production macOS apps should ship with Hardened Runtime enabled. This is a security regression.\n\n**Fix:** Set to `YES`. Note: requires proper code signing for entitlements.\n\n---\n\n## 2. HIGH Issues\n\n### Issue 4: Race Condition in BatteryService.refresh()\n**File:** `BatteryService.swift:31-39`\n\n```swift\nfunc refresh() {\n    DispatchQueue.global(qos: .background).async { [weak self] in\n        let detectedDevices = self?.detectDevices() ?? []\n        DispatchQueue.main.async {\n            self?.devices = detectedDevices  // Direct overwrite, no merge\n            ...\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n**Problem:** If `refresh()` is called while a previous call is still executing (e.g., user clicks rapidly, or timer fires while manual refresh in progress), devices array is directly overwritten rather than merged. Also `onDevicesUpdated` fires potentially mid-iteration if called from multiple threads.\n\n**Fix:** Add a synchronization mechanism (serial queue or lock) to prevent concurrent refreshes.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 5: Notification Authorization Error Silently Swallowed\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:22-28`\n\n```swift\nprivate func requestAuthorization() {\n    UNUserNotificationCenter.current().requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound, .badge]) { granted, error in\n        if let error = error {\n            print(\"Notification authorization error: \\(error)\")  // User never sees this\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n**Problem:** If notifications are denied, the user has no indication why low-battery alerts aren't appearing.\n\n**Fix:** Surface the error to user or at minimum store state to show \"notifications disabled\" in Settings.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 6: Notification Send Error Silently Swallowed\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:59-63`\n\n```swift\nUNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request) { error in\n    if let error = error {\n        print(\"Failed to send notification: \\(error)\")\n    }\n}\n```\n\n**Problem:** Same as above — failed notifications are invisible to user.\n\n**Fix:** Add logging or retry mechanism.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 7: Thread-Unsafe Access to NotifiedDevices\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:11, 36-43`\n\n```swift\nprivate var notifiedDevices: Set<String> = []  // Accessed from multiple threads\n\nfunc checkBatteryLevels(for devices: [DeviceBattery]) {\n    ...\n    if level <= notificationThreshold && !notifiedDevices.contains(device.id) {\n        sendNotification(for: device)\n        notifiedDevices.insert(device.id)  // Not thread-safe\n    }\n```\n\n**Problem:** `checkBatteryLevels` may be called from `BatteryService.refresh()` which runs on background thread, while UI may also access this. `Set<String>` is not thread-safe.\n\n**Fix:** Use a thread-safe collection or synchronization primitive.\n\n---\n\n## 3. MEDIUM Issues\n\n### Issue 8: Outdated Image Resizing API\n**File:** `MagicMouseBatteryApp.swift:57-66`\n\n```swift\nresizedImage.lockFocus()\nimage.draw(in: NSRect(origin: .zero, size: resizedImage.size),\n          from: NSRect(origin: .zero, size: image.size),\n          operation: .sourceOver,\n          fraction: 1.0)\nresizedImage.unlockFocus()\n```\n\n**Problem:** `lockFocus`/`unlockFocus` is deprecated. Modern approach uses `NSImage.draw(in:name:extensions:)` or better yet, use SF Symbols or proper asset handling.\n\n**Fix:** Use modern image resizing or SF Symbols for the battery icon.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 9: Unused Computed Property\n**File:** `DeviceBatteryView.swift:37-46`\n\n```swift\nprivate var batteryColor: Color { ... }  // Never used in the view\n```\n\n**Problem:** `batteryColor` is defined but not used — the view uses `.foregroundColor(batteryColor)` which would call this, but actually looking at the code, `BatteryLevelIndicator` handles its own coloring. Actually reviewing again, `batteryColor` IS used via `foregroundColor(batteryColor)` at line 10. This is a false positive.\n\n**Fix:** None needed (actually used).\n\n---\n\n### Issue 10: NotificationService Devices Property Redundant\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:12`\n\n```swift\nprivate var devices: [DeviceBattery] = []\n```\n\n**Problem:** `devices` is stored but only used within `checkBatteryLevels` to assign `self.devices = devices`. It could be used for additional logic but currently sits unused after assignment.\n\n**Fix:** Remove if not needed, or use for additional notification logic (e.g., track which devices already notified).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Easy to break.\n\n**Fix:** Use Xcode Gen's info template or single-source version.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 12: Magic Strings in UserDefaults Keys\n**File:** `NotificationService.swift:7`, `BatteryService.swift:130`\n\n```swift\nUserDefaults.standard.set(notificationThreshold, forKey: \"notificationThreshold\")\nUserDefaults.standard.set(isEnabled, forKey: \"launchAtLogin\")\n```\n\n**Problem:** Keys are repeated string literals — risk of typos.\n\n**Fix:** Use an enum or constants struct for UserDefaults keys.\n\n---\n\n### Issue 13: LaunchAtLoginService macOS Version Check Redundancy\n**File:** `BatteryService.swift:149-161`\n\n```swift\nprivate func updateLaunchAtLogin() {\n    if #available(macOS 13.0, *) {\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n**Problem:** `isEnabled` setter is called even on macOS 12 where `updateLaunchAtLogin` is a no-op.
